title: Gastric Distention and Helping Your Partner Intubate
next: Chapter 13, Lesson 5: Supraglottic airways, RSI, failed airways and special patients

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already ventilate with a BVM, suction, and insert OPAs and NPAs. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Prevent and spot gastric distention while you ventilate
  2. Predict a difficult airway and set up for your partner's intubation
  3. Help confirm and protect the tube on every move

Textbook: Chapter 13, PDF pages 1061–1157
slides.say: Welcome back. These last two lessons of Chapter thirteen cover the advanced end of airway care. First, the honest part: intubation, the drugs used for it, and surgical airways are beyond PCP scope in BC. So why learn them? Because you'll work right beside the advanced paramedic who does them, and the patient is safer when the assistant knows what's coming. Today we cover three things. First, gastric distention, which your own BVM technique can cause or prevent. Second, predicting a difficult airway and setting up for an intubation. And third, helping to confirm the tube and keep it in place.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。第十三章最后两节课讲气道处理的高级部分。先说实话：气管插管、插管用的药物和外科气道，在 BC 都超出 PCP 的执业范围。那为什么还要学？因为你就在做这些操作的高级救护员身边工作，助手越清楚接下来会发生什么，病人就越安全。今天讲三件事：第一，胃胀气——你自己的球囊面罩手法既可能造成它，也可以预防它；第二，预判困难气道、为插管做好准备；第三，协助确认导管位置，并让它保持在位。

slides.title: Gastric distention: how it happens
slides.body:
Air meant for the lungs goes into the stomach

  • Causes: too much pressure, too fast, partly blocked airway
  • Most common in children, but common in adults too
  • Harm 1: regurgitation, then aspiration
  • Harm 2: stomach pushes the diaphragm up; lungs can't expand
  • Signs: belly getting bigger, bag harder to squeeze
slides.say: Any time you blow air into the mouth instead of straight into the trachea, some of it can go down the esophagus into the stomach. That's gastric distention. It happens when you squeeze too hard or too fast, or ventilate through an airway that's partly blocked. It's most common in children, but adults get it too. It matters for two reasons. First, a full stomach pushes its contents back up, and vomit at the back of the throat ends up in the lungs. That's aspiration. Second, the swollen stomach pushes the diaphragm up, so the lungs have less room. Watch for a growing belly and a bag that gets harder to squeeze.
slides.sayZh: 只要你是把气吹进嘴里、而不是直接吹进气管，就有一部分气可能顺着食管进到胃里，这就是胃胀气。捏得太用力、太快，或者气道部分堵塞时通气，都会发生。儿童最常见，成人也很常见。它要紧有两个原因：第一，胃满了，内容物会反流上来，咽喉后部的呕吐物很快就进了肺，这叫误吸；第二，胀大的胃把膈肌往上顶，肺能扩张的空间就小了。留意肚子越来越鼓、球囊越来越难捏。

slides.title: Prevent it with a better BVM
slides.body:
1. Reposition the airway; add an OPA or NPA
  2. Squeeze over 1 second, just until the chest rises
  3. Rate: adult 10–12/min; child and infant 12–20/min
  4. Use two-person BVM whenever you can
  5. Watch the chest rise and fall with every breath

Belly already tight? Have suction ready: vomiting may follow.
slides.say: The best treatment for gastric distention is not causing it. You learned these steps as an EMR; now you'll often be the one leading them. If the bag gets stiff, first reposition the head and jaw and add an oral or nasal airway, because a partly blocked airway sends air to the stomach. Squeeze each breath over one second, and stop as soon as the chest rises. Keep the rate right: ten to twelve a minute for an adult, twelve to twenty for a child or infant. Two-person BVM gives a better seal with less pressure. The textbook also lists cricoid pressure, a gentle press on the ring just below the Adam's apple. And if the belly is tight, have suction ready.
slides.sayZh: 治胃胀气最好的办法是别让它发生。这些步骤你当 EMR 时学过，现在你常常要带头做。球囊变硬时，先重新摆正头和下颌，加上口咽或鼻咽通气道，因为气道半堵时气就往胃里跑。每次通气用一秒钟捏，看到胸廓起伏就停。频率要对：成人每分钟十到十二次，儿童和婴儿十二到二十次。双人球囊面罩通气密封更好、需要的压力更小。教材还列了环状软骨压迫，就是轻压喉结正下方那个软骨环。如果肚子已经很鼓，把吸引器准备好。

slides.title: Gastric tubes: NG vs OG
slides.body:
NG (nose)OG (mouth)
Best forAwake, responsive patientsUnresponsive, no gag reflex
Never ifMidface or skull fractureSafer in facial trauma
Measurenose → ear → xiphoidmouth → ear → xiphoid
NoteCan spoil the BVM mask sealUsually placed after intubation

Confirm: inject 20–30 mL of air and listen over the stomach, or see gastric contents.
slides.say: When positive pressure ventilation will go on for a long time, or a swollen stomach is blocking ventilation, especially in children, the stomach can be emptied with a gastric tube and suction. It's an advanced skill, but knowing the logic helps you assist. A nasogastric, or NG, tube goes through the nose, and awake patients tolerate it better. Never use it with a midface or skull fracture, because it can pass through the fracture into the skull. An orogastric, or OG, tube goes through the mouth, so it's safer in facial trauma. It's for unresponsive patients with no gag reflex, usually after intubation.
slides.sayZh: 如果正压通气要持续很久，或者胃胀已经妨碍通气（尤其是儿童），可以插胃管加吸引把胃排空。这是高级技能，但懂得其中的道理，你才能协助好。鼻胃管（NG）经鼻插入，清醒病人比较能耐受；面中部骨折或颅骨骨折绝对不能用，因为管子可能顺着骨折处进入颅内。口胃管（OG）经口插入，面部外伤时更安全；它用于没有反应、没有呕吐反射的病人，通常在气管插管之后再放。

slides.q: You're bagging an unresponsive overdose patient. The abdomen is getting bigger and the bag is harder to squeeze. What should you do first?
options: Squeeze harder and faster to push past the resistance
Reposition the airway; give each breath over 1 second, just to chest rise
Press on the abdomen to push the air out
Stop ventilating until ALS arrives with a gastric tube
slides.say: Let's check. You're bagging an unresponsive overdose patient. The abdomen is getting bigger and the bag is harder to squeeze. What should you do first? A, squeeze harder and faster to push past the resistance. B, reposition the airway and give each breath over one second, just to chest rise. C, press on the abdomen to push the air out. D, stop ventilating until ALS arrives with a gastric tube. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来考一下：你正在给一位没有反应的药物过量病人捏球囊，肚子越来越大，球囊越来越难捏。你首先该做什么？A 捏得更用力、更快，冲过阻力；B 重新摆正气道，每次通气用一秒钟、捏到胸廓起伏就停；C 按压腹部把气挤出来；D 停止通气，等 ALS 带胃管来。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A stiff bag and a growing belly mean air is going into the stomach, so fix the cause: open the airway properly and slow down, giving just enough to see the chest rise. A makes it worse, because more pressure and speed push even more air into the stomach. C can make the patient vomit into an unprotected airway. D is dangerous: this patient needs your ventilations now.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。球囊发硬、肚子变大，说明气在往胃里跑，要从原因下手：把气道打开好、放慢速度，捏到刚看见胸廓起伏就够。A 会更糟，压力更大、速度更快只会把更多气推进胃里。C 可能让病人在没有保护的气道里呕吐。D 很危险，这位病人现在就需要你的通气。

slides.title: Basics first, then predict trouble
slides.body:
A tube never replaces good basics

Why advance?airway won't stay open, or O₂ and ventilation fail
MOANShard to BVMMask seal, Obese, Aged, No teeth, Stiff lungs
LEMONhard to intubateLook, 3-3-2, Mallampati, Obstruction, Neck
slides.say: A common mistake, especially in cardiac arrest, is jumping to an advanced airway too early and letting the basics slide. A tube never replaces good basic care. Patients need an advanced airway when the airway won't stay open, or when oxygenation and ventilation fail. Two memory aids predict trouble. MOANS predicts a hard BVM: mask seal problems, obesity, older age, no teeth, and stiff lungs. That one is yours: if any item fits, plan two-person BVM with an airway adjunct from the start. LEMON predicts a hard intubation: look at the outside, the three-three-two finger rule, the Mallampati view, obstruction, and neck mobility. If LEMON fails, plan B must be ready before anyone starts.
slides.sayZh: 一个常见错误，尤其在心跳骤停时，是过早上高级气道、把基础功夫丢了。导管永远替代不了做好基础处理。病人需要高级气道，是因为气道维持不住通畅，或者氧合和通气做不够。两个口诀帮你预判麻烦。MOANS 预测球囊面罩通气困难：面罩密封差、肥胖、高龄、没有牙、肺僵硬。这个口诀是你自己要用的：只要有一项符合，一开始就准备双人球囊面罩加气道辅助装置。LEMON 预测插管困难：看外观、三三二指法则、Mallampati 分级、梗阻、颈部活动度。LEMON 不过关，在任何人动手之前就必须备好 B 计划。

slides.title: Setting up the intubation kit
slides.body:
• Keep bagging with 100% O₂; SpO₂ above 95%
  • Suction on and within reach
  • Tubes: expected size, one bigger, one smaller
  • Cuff tested with 10 mL of air; bougie ready
  • Light: "bright, white, steady, tight"
  • Waveform ETCO₂, stethoscope, tube holder, backup device

Adult tubes: women 7.0–8.0 mm, men 7.5–8.5 mm (inside diameter).
slides.say: While your partner gets ready, your job is usually the BVM: one hundred percent oxygen, aiming for a saturation above ninety-five percent. Turn the suction on and keep it within reach, because vomit and secretions ruin the view. Many services use an intubation checklist, and you can run it out loud. Adult tubes are usually seven to eight millimetres for women and seven and a half to eight and a half for men, with one size bigger and one smaller set out too. The cuff is tested with ten millilitres of air. The laryngoscope light should be bright, white, steady and tight. Then have waveform capnography, a stethoscope, a tube holder and a backup airway ready.
slides.sayZh: 搭档做准备时，你通常负责球囊面罩：百分之百氧气，让血氧保持在九十五以上。打开吸引器、放在手边，因为呕吐物和分泌物会挡住视野。很多单位用插管检查清单，你可以大声逐项念。成人导管一般女性七到八毫米、男性七点五到八点五毫米，另外再备大一号和小一号。套囊用十毫升空气测试是否漏气。喉镜灯光要「亮、白、稳、紧」。再备好波形二氧化碳监测、听诊器、导管固定器和后备气道装置。

slides.title: Preoxygenate and position
slides.body:
• BVM with 100% O₂ for 2–3 minutes; SpO₂ close to 100%
  • High-flow nasal cannula can stay on during the attempt
  • Sniffing position: ear level with the sternum
  • Obese: pad under the shoulders and neck too
  • Possible spine injury: neutral, in-line; you hold the head
slides.say: Preoxygenation is the most important thing you add. During the attempt the patient isn't ventilated at all, so you fill the lungs with oxygen first, like topping up a scuba tank before a dive. Ventilate with one hundred percent oxygen for two to three minutes, getting the saturation as close to one hundred percent as you can. A high-flow nasal cannula can stay on during the attempt to keep oxygen flowing. Then position: folded towels under the head until the ear is level with the sternum. That's the sniffing position, and obese patients need padding under the shoulders and neck too. With a possible spine injury, there's no sniffing position; you hold the head neutral and in line.
slides.sayZh: 预充氧是你最重要的贡献。插管过程中病人完全得不到通气，所以要先把肺灌满氧，就像潜水前把气瓶充满。用百分之百氧气通气两到三分钟，血氧尽量接近百分之百。插管时可以留着一根高流量鼻导管，让氧气继续流入。接下来是体位：在头下垫折叠毛巾，直到耳朵和胸骨齐平，这就是嗅物位；肥胖病人肩颈下也要垫。怀疑脊柱损伤就不能用嗅物位，由你手法固定头部，保持中立、轴线位。

slides.title: During the attempt: watch the clock
slides.body:
One attempt: 30 seconds max

  • Clock starts when the BVM stops; ends when the tube ventilates
  • Call out the time and any SpO₂ drop
  • Over 30 s: stop, re-oxygenate 30 s to 1 min, then retry
  • You may be asked for BURP: thyroid cartilage back, up, right
  • Cardiac arrest: compressions don't stop for the tube
slides.say: During the attempt, you're the timekeeper and the safety officer. One attempt should take no more than thirty seconds, counted from the moment the bag comes off to the moment the tube is ventilating. Watch the monitor and call out the time and any drop in saturation. At thirty seconds the attempt stops, and you re-oxygenate with one hundred percent oxygen for thirty seconds to a minute before another try. Your partner may ask you for BURP: backward, upward and rightward pressure on the thyroid cartilage to improve the view. And in cardiac arrest, compressions never stop for the tube; BC keeps every pause in CPR under five seconds.
slides.sayZh: 插管过程中，你是计时员，也是安全员。一次尝试不超过三十秒，从拿开球囊那一刻算起，到通过导管恢复通气为止。盯着监护仪，报时间、报任何血氧下降。到了三十秒就停，用百分之百氧气再充氧三十秒到一分钟，然后再试。搭档可能要你做 BURP：对甲状软骨施加向后、向上、向右的压力，改善视野。心跳骤停时，按压绝不为插管停下；BC 要求每次 CPR 中断都不超过五秒。

slides.q: Your partner is intubating. At 25 seconds the SpO₂ has fallen from 97% to 88% and the tube isn't in yet. What do you do?
options: Stay quiet so you don't distract your partner
Call out the time and SpO₂; get ready to resume BVM with 100% O₂
Squeeze the BVM into the open mouth while the blade is in
Turn off the suction to reduce the noise
slides.say: Here's an assistant's decision. Your partner is intubating. At twenty-five seconds, the saturation has fallen from ninety-seven to eighty-eight percent, and the tube isn't in yet. What do you do? A, stay quiet so you don't distract your partner. B, call out the time and the saturation, and get ready to resume BVM with one hundred percent oxygen. C, squeeze the BVM into the open mouth while the blade is in. D, turn off the suction to reduce the noise. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道助手决策题：你的搭档正在插管，到第二十五秒，血氧从百分之九十七掉到八十八，导管还没插进去。你怎么做？A 保持安静，免得干扰搭档；B 报出时间和血氧，准备用百分之百氧气恢复球囊面罩通气；C 在喉镜片还在嘴里时对着张开的嘴捏球囊；D 关掉吸引器减少噪音。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Watching the clock and the monitor, and speaking up, is your job. A falling saturation, or reaching thirty seconds, means the attempt stops and you re-oxygenate with the BVM and one hundred percent oxygen. A is wrong, because silence lets the patient become hypoxic. C is wrong, because you can't ventilate properly around a laryngoscope blade. D is wrong, because suction stays on during every attempt.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。盯着时间和监护仪、及时说出来，就是你的职责。血氧下降或到了三十秒，这次尝试就要停下，用球囊面罩和百分之百氧气重新充氧。A 错，你不出声，病人就会缺氧。C 错，喉镜片在嘴里时没法有效通气。D 错，每次尝试时吸引器都要开着。

slides.title: Confirming the tube
slides.body:
You findIt means
Waveform ETCO₂, equal breath sounds, quiet stomachIn the trachea
No waveform, gurgling over the stomach, no lung soundsEsophagus: tube out, suction, re-oxygenate
Breath sounds on the right onlyToo deep: right mainstem
  • At least 2 methods; one must be ETCO₂
  • Mist in the tube, esophageal bulb: not reliable
slides.say: Now the most important minute. A tube in the esophagus that nobody notices is a fatal error, so no single test is enough. Use at least two methods, and one must be ETCO2, ideally waveform capnography. Seeing the tube pass the vocal cords comes first. Then you may be the one listening: the stomach should be silent, and both sides of the chest at the midaxillary line should sound equal. Gurgling over the stomach, no lung sounds and no waveform mean the esophagus: the tube comes out, you suction, and you re-oxygenate. Sounds only on the right mean the tube is too deep, in the right mainstem bronchus. Mist in the tube proves nothing.
slides.sayZh: 接下来是最关键的一分钟。导管进了食管却没人发现，是致命错误，所以单靠一种检查不够。至少用两种方法，其中一种必须是呼气末二氧化碳，最好是波形监测。看到导管通过声带是第一步。然后听诊的可能就是你：上腹应该安静，两侧腋中线的呼吸音应该对称。上腹咕噜响、肺部没声音、没有波形，说明在食管：拔管、吸引、重新充氧。只有右侧有呼吸音，说明插太深，进了右主支气管。管内起雾什么也证明不了。

slides.title: Protecting the tube on the move
slides.body:
• A hand stays on the tube until it's secured
  • Note the depth mark (adults about 21–25 cm at the lips)
  • Bite block; head movement shifts the tip up to 5 cm
  • Reconfirm after every move, and on arrival
  • Bag suddenly stiff? Stomach, esophagus, tension pneumothorax
slides.say: Getting the tube in is only half the job. Tubes slip out easily, and a second intubation is usually harder, so a hand stays on the tube until it's secured, and you still support it while you bag. The depth mark is noted; in adults it's usually twenty-one to twenty-five centimetres at the lips. A bite block stops the patient biting the tube. Bending or extending the head can move the tip as much as five centimetres, so a collar and head blocks help on the road. Placement is rechecked and documented after every move and on arrival. And if the bag suddenly gets stiff, think stomach, esophagus, or tension pneumothorax.
slides.sayZh: 导管插进去只完成了一半。导管很容易滑脱，第二次插管通常更难，所以固定好之前手不能离开导管，固定后通气时也要扶着。记下导管刻度，成人在嘴唇处一般是二十一到二十五厘米。放牙垫，防止病人咬管。头部屈伸可以让管尖移动多达五厘米，所以转运中颈托和头部固定块会有帮助。每次搬动后和到达医院时，都要重新确认并记录。如果球囊突然变硬，想到胃胀气、导管进了食管或张力性气胸。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
1. Before: MOANS check, two-person BVM, suction on
  2. Preoxygenate 2–3 min; run the kit checklist; position
  3. During: keep time, watch SpO₂, BURP or in-line hold if asked
  4. After: listen, watch ETCO₂, hold the tube, reconfirm on moves
  5. Document what you did, saw and when
slides.say: So what does a PCP actually do when the advanced airway comes out? Before, you assess with MOANS, run a good two-person BVM, and have suction ready. Then you preoxygenate for two to three minutes, run the equipment checklist, and position the head. During the attempt, you keep time, watch the saturation, and apply BURP or hold the head in line if asked. Afterwards, you help listen, watch the waveform, keep a hand on the tube, and reconfirm after every move. Finally, document your part: what you did, what you saw, and when. A calm, prepared assistant makes the whole team safer.
slides.sayZh: 那么，当要上高级气道时，PCP 实际做什么？之前：用 MOANS 评估，做好双人球囊面罩通气，准备好吸引器。然后预充氧两到三分钟，逐项核对器材清单，摆好头位。插管时：计时、盯血氧，需要时做 BURP 或手法保持头部轴线。之后：协助听诊、看波形、扶住导管，每次搬动后重新确认。最后记录你那部分：你做了什么、看到了什么、什么时间。一个冷静、准备充分的助手，会让整个团队更安全。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• An unnoticed esophageal tube kills: trust ETCO₂, not hope
  • ETCO₂ suddenly flat: think tube out first
  • SpO₂ can read falsely high: watch the patient
  • Patient fighting the tube? Never pull it; tell your partner
  • Suction down the tube only if secretions block ventilation
slides.say: Here's what's new to watch out for. An esophageal tube that nobody notices is fatal, so trust the waveform, not hope. If the ETCO2 suddenly goes flat, assume the tube is out until you prove otherwise. The pulse oximeter can read falsely high, so watch the patient's colour, heart rate and chest rise. If an intubated patient wakes up and fights the tube, never pull it out yourself. It's rarely removed in the field, and getting it back in may be impossible, so tell your partner. And suctioning down the tube can trigger dangerous heart rhythms, so it's done only when secretions block ventilation, with preoxygenation, monitoring, and short passes.
slides.sayZh: 下面是你要新注意的事。导管进了食管而没人发现是致命的，要相信波形，不要靠侥幸。呼气末二氧化碳突然变成一条平线，先当作导管脱出，直到证明不是。血氧仪可能读数假性偏高，要看病人的肤色、心率和胸廓起伏。插管病人醒来和导管对抗时，绝不要自己把管拔掉：院前很少拔管，拔了可能再也插不回去，要告诉搭档。还有，经导管吸痰可能诱发危险的心律失常，只有分泌物堵到妨碍通气时才做，要先预充氧、全程监测、每次时间要短。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Cardiac arrest: compression pauses under 5 seconds
  • CPR: avoid hyperventilation
  • Suction: adult 10–15 s, child 10 s, infant 5 s
  • Opioid overdose: consider two-person BVM (all levels)
  • No endotracheal drug route in BC EMR/PCP scope

The book calls the tube a last-resort drug route; that's not a BC EMR/PCP option.
slides.say: A few BC points for the exam. In BC cardiac arrest care, pauses in compressions stay under five seconds, and the guideline says to avoid hyperventilation, which also protects the stomach. BC suction limits are ten to fifteen seconds in an adult, ten in a child, and five in an infant. The BC opioid overdose protocol asks every licence level to consider two-person BVM, which is MOANS in action. And the book mentions the tracheal tube as a last-resort route for drugs; in BC, the EMR and PCP scope has no endotracheal drug route. The written exam can still ask textbook facts, like the thirty-second rule, so know those too.
slides.sayZh: 几个 BC 考点。BC 的心跳骤停处理中，按压中断不超过五秒，指南还要求避免过度通气，这同时也保护了胃。BC 的吸引时限是成人十到十五秒、儿童十秒、婴儿五秒。BC 阿片类过量流程要求所有执照级别都考虑双人球囊面罩通气，这正是 MOANS 的实际应用。书上提到气管导管可作为最后手段的给药途径；在 BC，EMR 和 PCP 的范围里没有气管内给药。笔试仍可能考教材知识，比如三十秒规则，所以这些也要掌握。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Prevent distention: open airway, 1 second, stop at chest rise
  2. Set up well: MOANS/LEMON, suction, preoxygenate 2–3 min
  3. Confirm with 2+ methods incl. ETCO₂; reconfirm on every move

Next: supraglottic airways, RSI, failed airways and special patients
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: prevent gastric distention. Open the airway well, squeeze over one second, and stop at chest rise. Two: set your partner up for success. Check MOANS and LEMON, have suction on, preoxygenate for two to three minutes, and keep the thirty-second clock. Three: confirm every tube with at least two methods, one of them ETCO2, and reconfirm after every move. Next lesson, we finish the chapter: supraglottic airways and what BC says about PCPs using them, drug-assisted intubation, the failed airway, and special patients. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，预防胃胀气：把气道打开好，每次捏一秒钟，看到胸廓起伏就停。二，帮搭档做好准备：评估 MOANS 和 LEMON，吸引器开着，预充氧两到三分钟，盯住三十秒计时。三，每根导管都用至少两种方法确认，其中一种是呼气末二氧化碳，每次搬动后都重新确认。下节课我们讲完本章：声门上气道以及 BC 对 PCP 使用它们的说法、药物辅助插管、插管失败的气道，还有特殊病人。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
